items.stem: A CI job runs Claude Code to check a pull request. The job must restrict the run to the Read and Grep tools. A failed run must fail the job. Which command setup meets both constraints?
options: Run claude -p with --allowedTools set to Read and Grep, then check the exit status.
Run claude -p with --json-schema, which limits the tools that the run can use.
Run claude -p with --tools set to Read and Grep, then check the exit status in the next CI step.
Run claude -p with --tools set to Read and Grep, check the exit status, and store every transcript in a database.
items.rationale: The --tools flag restricts which built-in tools exist for the run. The exit status tells the CI step whether the run succeeded.
items.trap: An --allowedTools list looks like a restriction, but the flag only lets the listed tools run without a prompt.

items.stem: A script runs Claude Code and reads one typed field from the reply. The script must also record the total cost of each run. Which setup meets both constraints?
options: Run with --output-format json and --json-schema, then read structured_output and total_cost_usd.
Parse the free-text reply with a pattern match, and skip the cost field.
Run with --output-format json and --json-schema, and store every full transcript in a database.
Run with --tools set to a fixed list, and read the per-model breakdown from the --tools output.
items.rationale: The json output format with a schema returns typed fields in structured_output. The JSON output also includes total_cost_usd for each run.
items.trap: A pattern match on free text looks simple, but it gives the script no typed field and no cost value.

items.stem: A team wants one credential for six repositories that run comment-triggered workflows. The credential must not depend on the subscription of one person. Select two actions that meet the constraint.
options: Run the setup-token command, and store the OAuth token as one organization-level secret.
Create an API key in the Claude Console for the shared secret.
Set the use_bedrock input to true, which shares one credential across repositories.
Store one organization-level Actions secret that all six repositories share.
items.rationale: The OAuth token is tied to one subscription, but an API key from the Claude Console can serve a shared secret. An organization-level Actions secret lets the repositories share one stored copy.
items.trap: An OAuth token from the setup command looks easy to share, but it is tied to the subscription of one person.
